nodes.body: Which intervention or mechanism produces the reported experimental effect?

nodes.title: Choose construct and controls
nodes.body: The spontaneous deamination of cytosine is a major source of C•G to T•A transitions, which account for half of known human pathogenic point mutations.

nodes.title: Run assays against controls
nodes.body: The ability to efficiently convert target A•T base pairs to G•C therefore could advance the study and treatment of genetic diseases.

nodes.title: Primary reported result
nodes.body: Extensive directed evolution and protein engineering resulted in seventh-generation ABEs (e.g., ABE7.10), that convert target A•T to G•C base pairs efficiently (~50% in human cells) with very high product purity (typically ≥ 99.9%) and very low rates of indels (typically ≤ 0.1%).

nodes.title: Published conclusion
nodes.body: Together with our previous base editors, ABEs advance genome editing by enabling the direct, programmable introduction of all four transition mutations without double-stranded DNA cleavage.
